title: Exposure Governor Protocol and Stakeholder Sociology (wip)
content:
Status: working sketch. Goal: provide a lightweight operational protocol for small-batch exposures (micro-exposures) that balances metric sensitivity, stakeholder trust, and rapid rollback. This doc focuses on two things that often get missed: (1) an exposure ‘governor’ pattern (automated throttle + human escalation) and (2) a simple mental model for the cross-functional sociology — who needs what signal when and how to phrase communications so teams act quickly and coherently.

Why this exists (short):
- We keep seeing canaries fail not from bad models but from unclear owner expectations and noisy signals.
- Traditional percent-based canaries are brittle for multi-model flows (rerankers, fallback routing).
- Small product changes need faster feedback loops without over-alerting SRE or confusing PMs.

Core concepts (plain language):
- Exposure Governor: a single control that enforces an exposure budget (traffic %, safety budget, alert budget) and automatically reduces exposure when pre-defined safety signals cross thresholds. The governor is both automated (policy) and social (owners get notified and must re-authorize increases).
- Micro-exposure: short-lived, low-fraction traffic slice used to validate behavioral/quality assumptions, not revenue experiments. Typical window 30–90 minutes.
- Steward: the person responsible for the experiment’s readiness and primary point-of-contact. Stewards are often PMs or product engineers.
- Observer: cross-functional role (SRE, ML infra, Console) who has permission to flip the governor and initiate rollback if automation fails.

Policy sketch (practical):
- Preflight: must have a steward, 1-line hypothesis, quick eval set (50–200 prompts), and telemetry plan (latency, reject-rate, top-3 user-facing errors). Attach simple evaluation artifacts (CSV).
- Activate micro-exposure at <= 0.5% traffic, 30m warmup. Governor tracks: TPS, p95 latency, error-rate, user-visible regression metric (e.g., CTR or relevance score delta), and safety score (classifier).
- Signal windows: short window (5m) for high-confidence infra signals (latency spikes), medium window (30m) for behavioral signals, long window (24h) for business metrics. Governor action is tiered by window.

Governor thresholds (example defaults — tune per product):
- Infra: p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline (5m) -> automatic throttle 50% and alert to SRE.
- Errors: API error rate > 1% absolute and > 3x baseline (5m) -> auto-cut to 0, page SRE.
- Behavioral: user-relevance delta worse by > 5% (30m) -> throttle to half, notify steward and product-observers.
- Safety classifier: precision drop in safe-class detection > 2% (30m) -> immediate quarantine and human review.

Signals to compute (SQL-ish examples for product telemetry):
- baseline_p95_latency: SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) FROM request_latency WHERE model = 'candidate' AND ts BETWEEN now()-interval '7d' AND now()-interval '1d';
- canary_error_rate_5m: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 500)/count(*) FROM requests WHERE model IN ('candidate') AND ts > now()-interval '5 minutes';
- relevance_delta_30m: WITH c AS (SELECT user_id, relevance_score FROM responses WHERE model='candidate' AND ts>now()-interval '30 minutes'), b AS (SELECT user_id, relevance_score FROM responses WHERE model='baseline' AND ts>now()-interval '30 minutes') SELECT avg(c.relevance_score)-avg(b.relevance_score) FROM c JOIN b USING (user_id);

Stakeholder sociology (who, what they care about, and sample message templates):
- Steward (Product/PM or Eng Owner): cares about hypothesis validation and quick interpretation. Gets: 30m summary (delta metrics + example failures), recommended next steps. Sample: "micro-exposure 0.5% -> relevance delta -3.8% (30m). Top failure pattern: truncated entity extraction for invoice-type queries. Recommend rollback to baseline; steward sign-off required to re-enable and run focused prompt set."
- SRE/Infra: cares about infrastructure safety and SLOs. Gets infra-only page and auto actions. Sample: "AUTO: Governor throttled micro-exposure for model X due to p95 latency +48% (5m). Action: auto-throttle 50%. Please triage if persistent."
- Data/ML Research: wants edge cases and example inputs. Gets 50 worst-scoring examples, sample tokens, classifier scores.
- Legal/Trust (when required): summary of potential policy hits and whether quarantine engaged.

Escalation flow (play-by-play):
1) Governor triggers automated throttle (log an event with policy id).
2) Immediate Slack alert to (#exposure-alerts) channel with short context + link to artifacts.
3) Steward must acknowledge within 15 minutes with either: a) request human hold (freeze), b) request rollback, c) request further monitor (must supply why regression is acceptable). If no ack -> escalate to observer -> auto-cut to 0.
4) Post-mortem template auto-created if exposure lasted > 2 hours or governor forced rollback.

Small ceremony suggested (time-boxed):
- Activation checklist (5 items, 5 min): steward, hypothesis line, eval set attached, preflight telemetry hooks validated, rollback owner set.
- 30m sync: quick async report to stakeholders (steward posts short TL;DR in channel).
- Debrief: 1-hour debrief only if significant signal or >2% exposure needed.

Failure mode matrix (brief):
- False positive infra alert -> unnecessary rollback -> remedy: add smoothed baseline + cooldown for repeated infra flapping.
- Noisy behavioral signal -> guard: require both direction (magnitude + consistency across deciles) before auto-cut to 0.
- Slow owner response -> escalate and auto-fallback after configured TTL (default 15m).

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- Decide default TTLs per product (PMs + Console owners to propose templates).
- Implement small input-sampling hook that returns the 10 most informative failing prompts to Slack on throttle. (Rina + infra pairing).
- Add one-click rollback play in console to attach post-mortem template and set embargo for re-activation. (Liam + Console eng).

Quick annex: sample Slack alert text (for automation):
- "AUTOGOV: micro-exposure 'search-reranker-v2' throttled to 25% (was 0.5%) — reason: p95 latency +52% (5m). Steward: Priya Nair. Link: <artifact>. Ack required in 15m or auto-cut to 0"

Notes to self / meeting seeds:
- We should pilot this with two product teams: search reranker (latency sensitive) and inbox summarization (behavior sensitive).
- Keep governor policy parameterized and store defaults in repo so each product can opt-in with a PR.
- Avoid too many human gates on trivial regressions — aim for >95% of automation for infra signals, more human-in-the-loop for behavioral/safety signals.

If you’re reading this and want to volunteer to pilot, ping me (Priya). I’ll spin up a very small runbook + the slack alert template and work with Console to add the one-click rollback endpoint.

Revision history: 2025-11-03 initial sketch; 2025-12-11 added SQL samples and escalation TTLs; 2026-02-12 adjusted thresholds per demo with search reranker team.
